links.comparator_used: Raw FHIR JSON serialisation (also compared Markdown Table and Chronological Timeline) across five open-weight models
links.outcome: Medication reconciliation F1 on 200 synthetic patients (4,000 inference runs)
links.effect: Clinical Narrative outperformed Raw JSON by up to 19 F1 points for Mistral-7B (r = 0.617, p < 10^-10) in models up to 8B; the advantage reversed at 70B, where Raw JSON achieved the best mean F1 of 0.9956.
links.tradeoff: In all 20 model and strategy combinations mean precision exceeded mean recall, so omission of active medications was the dominant failure mode. Smaller models plateaued at roughly 7-10 concurrent active medications, underserving polypharmacy patients.
links.quote: We find that serialisation strategy has a large, statistically significant effect on performance for models up to 8B parameters: Clinical Narrative outperforms Raw JSON by up to 19 F1 points for Mistral-7B (r = 0.617, p < 10^{-10}).

links.comparator_used: Instruction-tuned general-purpose models (e.g., Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B) used on the same task
links.effect: BioMistral-7B, a domain-pretrained model without instruction tuning, produced zero usable output in all conditions.
links.quote: BioMistral-7B, a domain-pretrained model without instruction tuning, produces zero usable output in all conditions, showing that domain pretraining alone is not sufficient for structured extraction.
